title: OTP requested "to verify documents" vs. HR asking the candidate to upload documents to the onboarding portal
summary: Someone from Vistara Infotech's onboarding team calls a candidate who has accepted an offer, about verifying identity documents before joining. In the fraud case, the caller says an OTP has just been sent "for document verification" and asks the candidate to read it out. In the legitimate case, HR asks the candidate to log in to the onboarding portal themselves and upload the documents, mentioning that the portal sends a login OTP which the candidate enters on the portal and never shares with anyone, including HR.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a candidate who has accepted the offer; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: QA test engineer, CTC [AMOUNT_1] (₹4,00,000–₹8,00,000 per year), joining in one to two weeks.
Both calls mention PAN, Aadhaar, educational certificates, "verification", and an OTP.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks the candidate to disclose a one-time password received on their phone. Genuine entities do not ask for OTPs, and the OTP could authorise access or a transaction the candidate cannot see.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain the OTP to take over an account or authorise a transaction.
stable_facts: Caller claims documents must be "verified with the government database" before joining.
An OTP arrives on the candidate's phone during the call; the caller asks for it.
Caller already knows the candidate's name, role, and joining date.
Caller warns that joining is "on hold" until verification completes today.

legitimate.label_rationale: HR asks the candidate to upload documents themselves on the company portal and explicitly says never to share the portal OTP.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get documents uploaded before the joining date.
stable_facts: Portal: https://onboard.vistara-infotech.invalid, link also in the offer email.
The portal sends a login OTP to the candidate's registered mobile; the candidate types it on the portal.
Aadhaar may be uploaded masked (only last four digits visible).
HR will review the upload and call back only if something is unclear.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist, reassure ("it is only for verification"), or claim a new OTP is coming. They must not switch to asking for payments or app installs. The legitimate caller must not ask for the OTP or any password, PIN, or payment after the branch.

must_preserve: role, CTC, joining date, and document list identical across cases
_F request to read out the OTP at turn 7
_L self-upload with explicit "do not share the OTP
may_vary: whether Aadhaar or voter ID is mentioned
must_not_emit: real government databases or app names
real OTP message text or sender IDs
what the OTP was actually for

ambiguities: The word "OTP" appears in both cases. Only a request to disclose it is evidence.
The fraud caller knowing personal details is not evidence of legitimacy (C03).
The card never states what the OTP authorises; generation must not explain it.

Near jr_18 (net-banking credentials for a joining bonus): both harvest credentials during onboarding. Here the credential is an OTP and the pretext is identity verification; in jr_18 it is a net-banking login and the pretext is a payment credit. Flagged for deduplication review.

evidence_references.claim: Genuine entities never ask customers for OTP, PIN, CVV, or passwords (C01)
Impostors share a few real personal details to gain confidence (C03)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
